description: Married couple filing jointly, ages 45 and 43, combined wages and some bank interest; 22% bracket.
worked:
Line numbers are those of the 2025 Form 1040, its instructions' worksheets and Schedule 1-A; the figures are the 2026 ones from the federal file.
Filing status: married filing jointly.
Taxpayer: born 1981-03-08, age 45 at the end of 2026.
Spouse: born 1983-11-21, age 43 at the end of 2026.
Form 1040: line 1z wages 160,000; line 2b taxable interest 1,200.
Form 1040 line 9 total income = 160,000 + 1,200 = 161,200; line 10 adjustments 0; line 11a/11b adjusted gross income = 161,200.
Line 12e standard deduction = 32,200 (married filing jointly; no line 12d box: nobody 65 or older or blind).
Schedule 1-A Part V: nobody is 65 or older at the end of the year; senior deduction 0.
Line 14 = 32,200 + 0 = 32,200; line 15 taxable income = 161,200 - 32,200 = 129,000.
Form 1040 line 16 (regular tax): Tax Rate Schedule Y-1 (married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse) on 129,000: 10% x 24,800 = 2,480; 12% x (100,800 - 24,800) = 9,120; 22% x (129,000 - 100,800) = 6,204; total 17,804
Form 8960: lines 8 and 12 net investment income = 1,200; line 13 MAGI = 161,200; line 14 threshold = 250,000; line 15 = 161,200 - 250,000, zero or less, so 0; line 17 net investment income tax = 0.
Form 8959 Part I: line 1 Medicare wages (W-2 box 5) = line 4 = 160,000; line 5 = 250,000 (married filing jointly); line 6 = 160,000 - 250,000, zero or less, so 0; line 7 = 0.9% x 0 = 0 (additional Medicare tax).
Total tax = 17,804 regular + 0 net investment income tax + 0 additional Medicare tax = 17,804.
